title: Ecclesiastes 2:11
text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that it had cost me to do [them]; and behold, all was vanity and pursuit of the wind, and there was no profit under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:12
text: ¶And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly; for what shall the man [do] that cometh after the king? --that which hath already been done.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:13
text: And I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as light excelleth darkness.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:14
text: The wise man's eyes are in his head, and the fool walketh in darkness; but I myself also perceived that one event happeneth to them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:15
text: And I said in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool so will it happen even to me; and why was I then so wise? Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:16
text: For there shall be no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; because everything is already forgotten in the days which come. And how dieth the wise even as the fool?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:17
text: ¶And I hated life; for the work that is wrought under the sun was grievous unto me; for all is vanity and pursuit of the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:18
text: And I hated all my labour wherewith I had been toiling under the sun, because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:19
text: And who knoweth whether he will be a wise [man] or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour at which I have laboured, and wherein I have been wise under the sun. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:20
text: Then I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour wherewith I had laboured under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:21
text: For there is a man whose labour hath been with wisdom, and with knowledge, and with skill, and who leaveth it to a man that hath not laboured therein, to be his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:22
text: For what will man have of all his labour and of the striving of his heart, wherewith he hath wearied himself under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:23
text: For all his days are sorrows, and his travail vexation: even in the night his heart taketh no rest. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:24
text: There is nothing good for man, but that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 2:25
text: For who can eat, or who be eager, more than I?

title: Ecclesiastes 2:26
text: For he giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he giveth travail to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good in God's sight. This also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:1
text: ¶To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heavens:

title: Ecclesiastes 3:2
text: A time to be born, and a time to die; A time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:3
text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; A time to break down, and a time to build up;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:4
text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; A time to mourn, and a time to dance;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:5
text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; A time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:6
text: A time to seek, and a time to lose; A time to keep, and a time to cast away;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:7
text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; A time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:8
text: A time to love, and a time to hate; A time of war, and a time of peace.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:9
text: What profit hath he that worketh from that wherein he laboureth?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:10
text: I have seen the travail that God hath given to the sons of men to toil in.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:11
text: ¶He hath made everything beautiful in its time; also he hath set the world in their heart, so that man findeth not out from the beginning to the end the work that God doeth.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:12
text: I know that there is nothing good for them but to rejoice and to do well in their life;

title: Ecclesiastes 3:13
text: yea also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labour, it is the gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:14
text: I know that whatever God doeth, it shall be for ever; there is nothing to be added to it, nor anything to be taken from it; and God doeth [it], that [men] should fear before him.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:15
text: That which is was long ago, and that which is to be hath already been; and God bringeth back again that which is past.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:16
text: ¶And moreover I saw under the sun, that in the place of judgment, wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, wickedness was there.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:17
text: I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:18
text: I said in my heart, It is thus with the children of men, that God may prove them, and that they should see that they themselves are but beasts.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:19
text: For what befalleth the children of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other, and they have all one breath; and man hath no pre-eminence above the beast: for all is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:20
text: All go unto one place: all are of the dust, and all return to dust.

title: Ecclesiastes 3:21
text: Who knoweth the spirit of the children of men? Doth it go upwards? and the spirit of the beasts, doth it go downwards to the earth?

title: Ecclesiastes 3:22
text: And I have seen that there is nothing better than that man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:1
text: ¶And I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors was power, and they had no comforter.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:2
text: Then I praised the dead who are already dead more than the living who are yet alive;

title: Ecclesiastes 4:3
text: and more fortunate than both is he who hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:4
text: ¶And I saw all labour, and all success of work, that it is man's jealousy of his neighbour. This also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:5
text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:6
text: Better is a handful with quietness, than both hands full with labour and pursuit of the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:7
text: ¶And I returned and saw vanity under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:8
text: There is one [alone] and without a second; also he hath neither son nor brother: yet is there no end of all his labour, neither is his eye satisfied with riches, and [he saith not], For whom then am I labouring, and depriving my soul of good? This also is vanity and a grievous occupation.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:9
text: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:10
text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him that is alone when he falleth, and who hath not another to lift him up!

title: Ecclesiastes 4:11
text: Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one alone be warm?

title: Ecclesiastes 4:12
text: And if a [man] overpower the one, the two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:13
text: ¶Better is a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king, who knoweth no more how to be admonished.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:14
text: For out of the prison-house he came forth to reign, although he was born poor in his kingdom.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:15
text: I saw all the living that walk under the sun, with the child, the second, that should stand up in his stead.

title: Ecclesiastes 4:16
text: [There is] no end of all the people, of all that stood before them; those however that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a striving after the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:1
text: ¶Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and draw near to hear, rather than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they know not that they do evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:2
text: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thy heart be hasty to utter anything before God: for God is in the heavens, and thou upon earth; therefore let thy words be few.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:3
text: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business, and a fool's voice through a multitude of words.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:4
text: ¶When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:5
text: Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:6
text: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an inadvertence. Wherefore should God be wroth at thy voice, and destroy the work of thy hands?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:7
text: For in the multitude of dreams are vanities; so with many words: but fear God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:8
text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter; for a higher than the high is watching, and there are higher than they.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:9
text: ¶Moreover the earth is every way profitable: the king [himself] is dependent upon the field.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:10
text: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver, nor he that loveth abundance with increase. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:11
text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; and what profit is there to the owner thereof, except the beholding [of them] with his eyes?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:12
text: The sleep of the labourer is sweet, whether he have eaten little or much; but the fulness of the rich doth not suffer him to sleep.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:13
text: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt;

title: Ecclesiastes 5:14
text: or those riches perish by some evil circumstance, and if he have begotten a son, there is nothing in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:15
text: As he came forth from his mother's womb, naked shall he go away again as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:16
text: And this also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came so doth he go away, and what profit hath he, in having laboured for the wind?

title: Ecclesiastes 5:17
text: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and hath much vexation, and sickness, and irritation.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:18
text: ¶Behold what I have seen good and comely: [it is] to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labour wherewith [man] laboureth under the sun, all the days of his life which God hath given him: for that is his portion.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:19
text: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and power to eat thereof, and to take his portion and to rejoice in his labour: that is a gift of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 5:20
text: For he will not much remember the days of his life, because God answereth [him] with the joy of his heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:1
text: ¶There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it is frequent among men:

title: Ecclesiastes 6:2
text: one to whom God giveth riches, wealth, and honour, and he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this is vanity, and a sore evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:3
text: If a man beget a hundred [sons], and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, but his soul be not filled with good, and also he have no burial, I say an untimely birth is better than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:4
text: For it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness;

title: Ecclesiastes 6:5
text: moreover it hath not seen nor known the sun: this hath rest rather than the other.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:6
text: Yea, though he live twice a thousand years, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:7
text: ¶All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:8
text: For what advantage hath the wise above the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:9
text: Better is the seeing of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this also is vanity and pursuit of the wind.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:10
text: That which is hath already been named; and what man is, is known, and that he cannot contend with him that is mightier than he.

title: Ecclesiastes 6:11
text: ¶For there are many things that increase vanity: what is man advantaged?

title: Ecclesiastes 6:12
text: For who knoweth what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell man what shall be after him under the sun?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:1
text: ¶A [good] name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:2
text: It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: in that that is the end of all men, and the living taketh it to heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:3
text: Vexation is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:4
text: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools in the house of mirth.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:5
text: It is better for a man to hear the rebuke of the wise, than to hear the song of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:6
text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:7
text: ¶Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad, and a gift destroyeth the heart.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:8
text: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning; better is a patient spirit than a proud spirit.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:9
text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be vexed; for vexation resteth in the bosom of fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:10
text: Say not, How is it that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not inquire wisely concerning this.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:11
text: ¶Wisdom is as good as an inheritance, and profitable to them that see the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:12
text: For wisdom is a defence [as] money is a defence; but the excellency of knowledge is, [that] wisdom maketh them that possess it to live.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:13
text: Consider the work of God; for who can make straight what he hath made crooked?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:14
text: In the day of prosperity enjoy good, and in the day of adversity consider: God hath also set the one beside the other, to the end that man should find out nothing [of what shall be] after him.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:15
text: All [this] have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous [man] that perisheth by his righteousness, and there is a wicked [man] that prolongeth [his days] by his wickedness.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:16
text: Be not righteous overmuch; neither make thyself overwise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:17
text: Be not overmuch wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:18
text: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from that withdraw not thy hand: for he that feareth God cometh forth from them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:19
text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty [men] that are in a city.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:20
text: Surely there is not a righteous man upon earth, that doeth good and sinneth not.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:21
text: Also give not heed unto all words that are spoken, lest thou hear thy servant curse thee.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:22
text: For also thine own heart knoweth that oftentimes thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:23
text: ¶All this have I tried by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:24
text: Whatever hath been, is far off, and exceeding deep: who will find it out?

title: Ecclesiastes 7:25
text: I turned, I and my heart, to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom and reason, and to know wickedness to be folly, and foolishness to be madness;

title: Ecclesiastes 7:26
text: and I found more bitter than death the woman whose heart is nets and snares, [and] whose hands are bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:27
text: See this which I have found, saith the Preacher, [searching] one by one to find out the reason;

title: Ecclesiastes 7:28
text: which my soul yet seeketh, and I have not found: one man among a thousand have I found, but a woman among all those have I not found.

title: Ecclesiastes 7:29
text: Only see this which I have found: that God made man upright, but they have sought out many devices.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:1
text: ¶Who is as the wise? and who knoweth the explanation of things? A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face is changed.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:2
text: I [say], Keep the king's commandment, and [that] on account of the oath of God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:3
text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight; persist not in an evil thing: for he doeth whatever pleaseth him,

title: Ecclesiastes 8:4
text: because the word of a king is power; and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:5
text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing; and a wise man's heart knoweth time and manner.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:6
text: ¶For to every purpose there is time and manner. For the misery of man is great upon him;

title: Ecclesiastes 8:7
text: for he knoweth not that which shall be; for who can tell him how it shall be?

title: Ecclesiastes 8:8
text: There is no man who hath control over the spirit to retain the spirit; and no one hath control over the day of death; and there is no discharge in that war, neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:9
text: ¶All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when man ruleth man to his hurt.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:10
text: And I have also seen the wicked buried and going away; and such as had acted rightly went from [the] holy place, and were forgotten in the city. This also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:11
text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the children of men is fully set in them to do evil.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:12
text: Though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and prolong his [days], yet I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, because they fear before him;

title: Ecclesiastes 8:13
text: but it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong [his] days as a shadow, because he feareth not before God.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:14
text: ¶There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are righteous [men] unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; and there are wicked [men] to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:15
text: And I commended mirth, because there is nothing better for man under the sun than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry; for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God hath given him under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 8:16
text: When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth (for also there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes),

title: Ecclesiastes 8:17
text: then I saw that all [is] the work of God, [and] that man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because however man may labour to seek [it] out, yet doth he not find [it]; and even, if a wise [man] think to know [it], he shall not be able to find [it] out.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:1
text: ¶For all this I laid to my heart and [indeed] to investigate all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; man knoweth neither love nor hatred: all is before them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:2
text: All things [come] alike to all: one event to the righteous and to the wicked, to the good, and to the clean, and to the unclean, to him that sacrificeth and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:3
text: This is an evil among all that is done under the sun, that one thing befalleth all: yea, also the heart of the children of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live; and after that, [they have to go] to the dead.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:4
text: ¶For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:5
text: For the living know that they shall die; but the dead know not anything, neither have they any more a reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:6
text: Their love also, and their hatred, and their envy is already perished; neither have they any more for ever a portion in all that is done under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:7
text: Go, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God hath already accepted thy works.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:8
text: Let thy garments be always white, and let not thy head lack oil.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:9
text: Enjoy life with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity; for that is thy portion in life, and in thy labour wherein thou art labouring under the sun.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:10
text: Whatever thy hand findeth to do, do with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, whither thou goest.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:11
text: ¶I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to the intelligent, nor yet favour to men of knowledge; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:12
text: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are taken with the snare, like them are the children of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:13
text: ¶This also have I seen as wisdom under the sun, and it was great unto me.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:14
text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and encompassed it, and built great bulwarks against it:

title: Ecclesiastes 9:15
text: and there was found in it a poor wise man, who by his wisdom delivered the city; but no man remembered that poor man.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:16
text: Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength; but the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:17
text: The words of the wise are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

title: Ecclesiastes 9:18
text: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroyeth much good.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:1
text: ¶Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to stink [and] ferment; [so] a little folly is weightier than wisdom [and] honour.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:2
text: The heart of a wise [man] is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:3
text: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his sense faileth [him], and he saith to every one [that] he is a fool.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:4
text: ¶If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for quietness pacifieth great offences.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:5
text: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as an error [that] proceedeth from the ruler:

title: Ecclesiastes 10:6
text: folly is set in great dignities, but the rich sit in a low place.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:7
text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:8
text: He that diggeth a pit falleth into it; and whoso breaketh down a hedge, a serpent biteth him.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:9
text: Whoso removeth stones is hurt therewith; he that cleaveth wood is endangered thereby.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:10
text: If the iron be blunt, and one do not whet the edge, then must he apply more strength; but wisdom is profitable to give success.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:11
text: If the serpent bite before enchantment, then the charmer hath no advantage.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:12
text: ¶The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool swallow up himself.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:13
text: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:14
text: And the fool multiplieth words: [yet] man knoweth not what shall be; and what shall be after him, who will tell him?

title: Ecclesiastes 10:15
text: The labour of fools wearieth them, because they know not how to go to the city.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:16
text: ¶Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

title: Ecclesiastes 10:17
text: Happy art thou, O land, when thy king is a son of nobles, and thy princes eat in [due] season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

title: Ecclesiastes 10:18
text: By much sloth fulness the framework falleth in; and through idleness of the hands the house drippeth.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:19
text: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh life merry; but money answereth everything.

title: Ecclesiastes 10:20
text: Curse not the king, no, not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for the bird of the air will carry the voice, and that which hath wings will tell the matter.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:1
text: ¶Cast thy bread upon the waters; for thou shalt find it after many days.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:2
text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:3
text: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth; and if a tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:4
text: He that observeth the wind will not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds will not reap.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:5
text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, how the bones [grow] in the womb of her that is with child, even so thou knowest not the work of God who maketh all.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:6
text: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thy hand; for thou knowest not which shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:7
text: ¶Now the light is sweet, and pleasant is it to the eyes to see the sun;

title: Ecclesiastes 11:8
text: but if a man live many years, [and] rejoice in them all, yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many: all that cometh is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:9
text: Rejoice, young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thine eyes; but know that for all these [things] God will bring thee into judgment.

title: Ecclesiastes 11:10
text: Then remove discontent from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh; for childhood and youth are vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:1
text: ¶And remember thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw nigh, of which thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:2
text: before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars, be darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:3
text: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows are darkened,

title: Ecclesiastes 12:4
text: and the doors are shut toward the street; when the sound of the grinding is subdued, and they rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:5
text: they are also afraid of what is high, and terrors are in the way, and the almond is despised, and the grasshopper is a burden, and the caper-berry is without effect; (for man goeth to his age-long home, and the mourners go about the streets;)

title: Ecclesiastes 12:6
text: --before the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be shattered at the fountain, or the wheel be broken at the cistern;

title: Ecclesiastes 12:7
text: and the dust return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return unto God who gave it.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:8
text: ¶Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher: all is vanity.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:9
text: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; and he pondered, and sought out, [and] set in order many proverbs.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:10
text: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words; and that which was written is upright, words of truth.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:11
text: The words of the wise are as goads, and the collections [of them] as nails fastened in: they are given from one shepherd.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:12
text: And besides, my son, be warned by them: of making many books there is no end, and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:13
text: ¶Let us hear the end of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole of man.

title: Ecclesiastes 12:14
text: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good or whether it be evil.

title: Song of Solomon 1:1
text: ¶The song of songs, which is Solomon's.

title: Song of Solomon 1:2
text: ¶Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.

title: Song of Solomon 1:3
text: Thine ointments savour sweetly; Thy name is an ointment poured forth: Therefore do the virgins love thee.

title: Song of Solomon 1:4
text: Draw me, we will run after thee! --The king hath brought me into his chambers--We will be glad and rejoice in thee, We will remember thy love more than wine. They love thee uprightly.

title: Song of Solomon 1:5
text: I am black, but comely, daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.

title: Song of Solomon 1:6
text: Look not upon me, because I am black; Because the sun hath looked upon me. My mother's children were angry with me: They made me keeper of the vineyards; Mine own vineyard have I not kept.

title: Song of Solomon 1:7
text: ¶Tell me, thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest [thy flock], Where thou makest it to rest at noon; For why should I be as one veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?

title: Song of Solomon 1:8
text: If thou know not, thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds' booths.

title: Song of Solomon 1:9
text: I compare thee, my love, To a steed in Pharaoh's chariots.

title: Song of Solomon 1:10
text: Thy cheeks are comely with bead-rows, Thy neck with ornamental chains.

title: Song of Solomon 1:11
text: We will make thee bead-rows of gold With studs of silver.

title: Song of Solomon 1:12
text: ¶While the king is at his table, My spikenard sendeth forth its fragrance.

title: Song of Solomon 1:13
text: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved unto me; He shall pass the night between my breasts.

title: Song of Solomon 1:14
text: My beloved is unto me a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of Engedi.

title: Song of Solomon 1:15
text: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold, thou art fair: thine eyes are doves.

title: Song of Solomon 1:16
text: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant; Also our bed is green.

title: Song of Solomon 1:17
text: The beams of our houses are cedars, Our rafters are cypresses.

title: Song of Solomon 2:1
text: ¶I am a narcissus of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.

title: Song of Solomon 2:2
text: As the lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.

title: Song of Solomon 2:3
text: ¶As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons: In his shadow have I rapture and sit down; And his fruit is sweet to my taste.

title: Song of Solomon 2:4
text: He hath brought me to the house of wine, And his banner over me is love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:5
text: Sustain ye me with raisin-cakes, Refresh me with apples; For I am sick of love.

title: Song of Solomon 2:6
text: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.

title: Song of Solomon 2:7
text: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.

title: Song of Solomon 2:8
text: ¶The voice of my beloved! Behold, he cometh Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.

title: Song of Solomon 2:9
text: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young hart. Behold, he standeth behind our wall, He looketh in through the windows, Glancing through the lattice.

title: Song of Solomon 2:10
text: My beloved spake and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

title: Song of Solomon 2:11
text: For behold, the winter is past, The rain is over, it is gone:

title: Song of Solomon 2:12
text: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of singing is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;

title: Song of Solomon 2:13
text: The fig-tree melloweth her winter figs, And the vines in bloom give forth [their] fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away!

title: Song of Solomon 2:14
text: ¶My dove, in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the precipice, Let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

title: Song of Solomon 2:15
text: Take us the foxes, The little foxes, that spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in bloom.

title: Song of Solomon 2:16
text: My beloved is mine, and I am his; He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies,

title: Song of Solomon 2:17
text: Until the day dawn, and the shadows flee away. Turn, my beloved: be thou like a gazelle or a young hart, Upon the mountains of Bether.

title: Song of Solomon 3:1
text: ¶On my bed, in the nights, I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

title: Song of Solomon 3:2
text: I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broadways Will I seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

title: Song of Solomon 3:3
text: The watchmen that go about the city found me: --Have ye seen him whom my soul loveth?

title: Song of Solomon 3:4
text: --Scarcely had I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother's house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.

title: Song of Solomon 3:5
text: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake [my] love, till he please.

title: Song of Solomon 3:6
text: ¶Who is this, [she] that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant? ...

title: Song of Solomon 3:7
text: ¶Behold his couch, Solomon's own: Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty of Israel.

title: Song of Solomon 3:8
text: They all hold the sword, Experts in war; Each hath his sword upon his thigh Because of alarm in the nights.

title: Song of Solomon 3:9
text: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 3:10
text: Its pillars he made of silver, Its support of gold, Its seat of purple; The midst thereof was paved [with] love By the daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Solomon 3:11
text: Go forth, daughters of Zion, And behold king Solomon With the crown wherewith his mother crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.

title: Song of Solomon 4:1
text: ¶Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are doves behind thy veil; Thy hair is as a flock of goats, On the slopes of mount Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 4:2
text: Thy teeth are like a flock of shorn sheep, Which go up from the washing; Which have all borne twins, And none is barren among them.

title: Song of Solomon 4:3
text: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy speech is comely; As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples Behind thy veil.

title: Song of Solomon 4:4
text: Thy neck is like the tower of David, Built for an armoury: A thousand bucklers hang thereon, All shields of mighty men.

title: Song of Solomon 4:5
text: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, Which feed among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 4:6
text: Until the day dawn, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.

title: Song of Solomon 4:7
text: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.

title: Song of Solomon 4:8
text: ¶[Come] with me, from Lebanon, [my] spouse, With me from Lebanon, --Come, look from the top of Amanah, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions' dens, From the mountains of the leopards.

title: Song of Solomon 4:9
text: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, [my] spouse; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.

title: Song of Solomon 4:10
text: How fair is thy love, my sister, [my] spouse! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine ointments than all spices!

title: Song of Solomon 4:11
text: Thy lips, [my] spouse, drop [as] the honeycomb; Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:12
text: A garden enclosed is my sister, [my] spouse; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

title: Song of Solomon 4:13
text: Thy shoots are a paradise of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants;

title: Song of Solomon 4:14
text: Spikenard and saffron; Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

title: Song of Solomon 4:15
text: ¶A fountain in the gardens, A well of living waters, Which stream from Lebanon.

title: Song of Solomon 4:16
text: Awake, north wind, and come, [thou] south; Blow upon my garden, [that] the spices thereof may flow forth. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat its precious fruits.

title: Song of Solomon 5:1
text: ¶I am come into my garden, my sister, [my] spouse; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, beloved ones!

title: Song of Solomon 5:2
text: ¶I slept, but my heart was awake. The voice of my beloved! he knocketh: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, mine undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

title: Song of Solomon 5:3
text: --I have put off my tunic, how should I put it on? I have washed my feet, how should I pollute them? --

title: Song of Solomon 5:4
text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole [of the door]; And my bowels yearned for him.

title: Song of Solomon 5:5
text: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the lock.

title: Song of Solomon 5:6
text: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself; he was gone: My soul went forth when he spoke. I sought him, but I found him not; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

title: Song of Solomon 5:7
text: The watchmen that went about the city found me; They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

title: Song of Solomon 5:8
text: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, ...What will ye tell him? --That I am sick of love.

title: Song of Solomon 5:9
text: ¶What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, Thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than [another] beloved, That thou dost so charge us?

title: Song of Solomon 5:10
text: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

title: Song of Solomon 5:11
text: His head is [as] the finest gold; His locks are flowing, black as the raven;

title: Song of Solomon 5:12
text: His eyes are like doves by the water-brooks, Washed with milk, fitly set;

title: Song of Solomon 5:13
text: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, raised beds of sweet plants; His lips lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

title: Song of Solomon 5:14
text: His hands gold rings, set with the chrysolite; His belly is bright ivory, overlaid [with] sapphires;

title: Song of Solomon 5:15
text: His legs, pillars of marble, set upon bases of fine gold: His bearing as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars;

title: Song of Solomon 5:16
text: His mouth is most sweet: Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, yea, this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

title: Song of Solomon 6:1
text: ¶Whither is thy beloved gone, Thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside? And we will seek him with thee.

title: Song of Solomon 6:2
text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens and to gather lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 6:3
text: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies.

title: Song of Solomon 6:4
text: ¶Thou art fair, my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as troops with banners:

title: Song of Solomon 6:5
text: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats On the slopes of Gilead.

title: Song of Solomon 6:6
text: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep Which go up from the washing; Which have all borne twins, And none is barren among them.

title: Song of Solomon 6:7
text: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples Behind thy veil.

title: Song of Solomon 6:8
text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number:

title: Song of Solomon 6:9
text: My dove, mine undefiled, is but one; She is the only one of her mother, She is the choice one of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and they called her blessed; The queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

title: Song of Solomon 6:10
text: Who is she that looketh forth as the dawn, Fair as the moon, clear as the sun, Terrible as troops with banners?

title: Song of Solomon 6:11
text: ¶I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the verdure of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, Whether the pomegranates blossomed.

title: Song of Solomon 6:12
text: Before I was aware, My soul set me upon the chariots of my willing people.

title: Song of Solomon 6:13
text: Return, return, O Shulamite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. --What would ye look upon in the Shulamite? --As it were the dance of two camps.

title: Song of Solomon 7:1
text: ¶How beautiful are thy footsteps in sandals, O prince's daughter! The roundings of thy thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of an artist.

title: Song of Solomon 7:2
text: Thy navel is a round goblet, [which] wanteth not mixed wine; Thy belly a heap of wheat, set about with lilies;

title: Song of Solomon 7:3
text: Thy two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle;

title: Song of Solomon 7:4
text: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; Thine eyes, [like] the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose like the tower of Lebanon, Which looketh toward Damascus;

title: Song of Solomon 7:5
text: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the locks of thy head like purple; The king is fettered by [thy] ringlets!

title: Song of Solomon 7:6
text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, [my] love, in delights!

title: Song of Solomon 7:7
text: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to grape clusters.

title: Song of Solomon 7:8
text: I said, I will go up to the palm-tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof; And thy breasts shall indeed be like clusters of the vine, And the fragrance of thy nose like apples,

title: Song of Solomon 7:9
text: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine, ...That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, And stealeth over the lips of them that are asleep.

title: Song of Solomon 7:10
text: ¶I am my beloved's, And his desire is toward me.

title: Song of Solomon 7:11
text: --Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the fields; Let us lodge in the villages.

title: Song of Solomon 7:12
text: We will go up early to the vineyards, We will see if the vine hath budded, [If] the blossom is opening, And the pomegranates are in bloom: There will I give thee my loves.

title: Song of Solomon 7:13
text: The mandrakes yield fragrance; And at our gates are all choice fruits, new and old: I have laid them up for thee, my beloved.

title: Song of Solomon 8:1
text: ¶Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! Should I find thee without, I would kiss thee; And they would not despise me.

title: Song of Solomon 8:2
text: I would lead thee, bring thee into my mother's house; Thou wouldest instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.

title: Song of Solomon 8:3
text: His left hand would be under my head, And his right hand embrace me.

title: Song of Solomon 8:4
text: I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem, ...Why should ye stir up, why awake [my] love, till he please?

title: Song of Solomon 8:5
text: ¶Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? I awoke thee under the apple-tree: There thy mother brought thee forth; There she brought thee forth [that] bore thee.

title: Song of Solomon 8:6
text: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol: The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, Flames of Jah.

title: Song of Solomon 8:7
text: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither do the floods drown it: Even if a man gave all the substance of his house for love, It would utterly be contemned.

title: Song of Solomon 8:8
text: ¶We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for? --

title: Song of Solomon 8:9
text: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver; And if she be a door, We will enclose her with boards of cedar.

title: Song of Solomon 8:10
text: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers; Then was I in his eyes as one that findeth peace.

title: Song of Solomon 8:11
text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon: He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand silver-pieces.

title: Song of Solomon 8:12
text: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: The thousand [silver-pieces] be to thee, Solomon; And to the keepers of its fruit, two hundred.

title: Song of Solomon 8:13
text: ¶Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken to thy voice: Let me hear [it].

title: Song of Solomon 8:14
text: Haste, my beloved, And be thou like a gazelle or a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.

title: Isaiah 1:1
text: ¶The vision of Isaiah the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

title: Isaiah 1:2
text: ¶Hear, [ye] heavens, and give ear, [thou] earth! for Jehovah hath spoken: I have nourished and brought up children; and they have rebelled against me.

title: Isaiah 1:3
text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib; Israel doth not know, my people hath no intelligence.

title: Isaiah 1:4
text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that corrupt themselves! They have forsaken Jehovah; they have despised the Holy One of Israel; they are turned away backward.

title: Isaiah 1:5
text: Why should ye be smitten any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

title: Isaiah 1:6
text: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in him; wounds, and weals, and open sores: they have not been dressed, nor bound up, nor mollified with oil.

title: Isaiah 1:7
text: Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; your land, strangers eat it up in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

title: Isaiah 1:8
text: And the daughter of Zion is left, as a booth in a vineyard, as a night-lodge in a cucumber-garden, as a besieged city.

title: Isaiah 1:9
text: Unless Jehovah of hosts had left us a very small residue, we should have been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

title: Isaiah 1:10
text: ¶Hear the word of Jehovah, rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, people of Gomorrah!

title: Isaiah 1:11
text: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Jehovah. I am sated with burnt-offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and in the blood of bullocks, and of lambs, and of he-goats I take no pleasure.

title: Isaiah 1:12
text: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this from your hand--to tread my courts?

title: Isaiah 1:13
text: Bring no more vain oblations! Incense is an abomination unto me, --new moon and sabbath, the calling of convocations--wickedness and the solemn meeting I cannot bear.

title: Isaiah 1:14
text: Your new moons and your set feasts my soul hateth: they are a burden to me; I am wearied of bearing [them].

title: Isaiah 1:15
text: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you; yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

title: Isaiah 1:16
text: ¶Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; --cease to do evil,

title: Isaiah 1:17
text: learn to do well: seek judgment, gladden the oppressed, do justice to the fatherless, plead for the widow.

title: Isaiah 1:18
text: Come now, let us reason together, saith Jehovah: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

title: Isaiah 1:19
text: If ye be willing and hearken, ye shall eat the good of the land;

title: Isaiah 1:20
text: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of Jehovah hath spoken.

title: Isaiah 1:21
text: ¶How is the faithful city become a harlot! It was full of judgment; righteousness used to lodge in it, but now murderers.

title: Isaiah 1:22
text: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine is mixed with water:

title: Isaiah 1:23
text: thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves; every one loveth presents, and hunteth after rewards; they judge not the fatherless, and the cause of the widow cometh not unto them.

title: Isaiah 1:24
text: Therefore saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah! I will ease me of mine adversaries, and avenge me of mine enemies.

title: Isaiah 1:25
text: And I will turn my hand upon thee, and will thoroughly purge away thy dross, and take away all thine alloy;

title: Isaiah 1:26
text: and I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning. Afterwards thou shalt be called, Town of righteousness, Faithful city.

title: Isaiah 1:27
text: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and they that return of her with righteousness.

title: Isaiah 1:28
text: But the ruin of the transgressors and of the sinners [shall be] together; and they that forsake Jehovah shall be consumed.

title: Isaiah 1:29
text: For they shall be ashamed of the terebinths that ye have desired, and ye shall blush for the gardens that ye have chosen.

title: Isaiah 1:30
text: For ye shall be as a terebinth whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water.

title: Isaiah 1:31
text: And the strong shall be for tow, and his work a spark; and they shall both burn together, and there shall be none to quench [them].

title: Isaiah 2:1
text: ¶The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:2
text: And it shall come to pass in the end of days, [that] the mountain of Jehovah's house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be lifted up above the hills; and all the nations shall flow unto it.

title: Isaiah 2:3
text: And many peoples shall go and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and Jehovah's word from Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 2:4
text: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall reprove many peoples; and they shall forge their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning-knives: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

title: Isaiah 2:5
text: House of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 2:6
text: ¶For thou hast cast off thy people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled [with what comes] from the east, and use auguries like the Philistines, and ally themselves with the children of foreigners.

title: Isaiah 2:7
text: And their land is full of silver and gold, and there is no end of their treasures: their land also is full of horses, and there is no end of their chariots.

title: Isaiah 2:8
text: And their land is full of idols; they bow themselves down to the work of their own hands, to that which their fingers have made.

title: Isaiah 2:9
text: And the mean man shall be bowed down, and the great man shall be brought low: and do not thou forgive them!

title: Isaiah 2:10
text: ¶Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty.

title: Isaiah 2:11
text: The lofty eyes of man shall be brought low, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day.

title: Isaiah 2:12
text: For there shall be a day of Jehovah of hosts upon everything proud and lofty, and upon everything lifted up, and it shall be brought low;

title: Isaiah 2:13
text: and upon all the cedars of Lebanon, high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan;

title: Isaiah 2:14
text: and upon all the lofty mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up;

title: Isaiah 2:15
text: and upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall;

title: Isaiah 2:16
text: and upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant works of art.

title: Isaiah 2:17
text: And the loftiness of man shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; and Jehovah alone shall be exalted in that day:

title: Isaiah 2:18
text: and the idols shall utterly pass away.

title: Isaiah 2:19
text: And they shall go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall arise to terrify the earth.

title: Isaiah 2:20
text: In that day men shall cast away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made [each] for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

title: Isaiah 2:21
text: to go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the fissures of the cliffs, from before the terror of Jehovah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall arise to terrify the earth.

title: Isaiah 2:22
text: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for what account is to be made of him?

title: Isaiah 3:1
text: ¶For behold, the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, will take away from Jerusalem and from Judah stay and staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,

title: Isaiah 3:2
text: the mighty man and the man of war, the judge and the prophet, and the diviner and the elder,

title: Isaiah 3:3
text: the captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the clever among artificers, and the one versed in enchantments.

title: Isaiah 3:4
text: And I will appoint youths as their princes, and children shall rule over them.

title: Isaiah 3:5
text: And the people shall be oppressed one by the other, and each by his neighbour; the child will be insolent against the elder, and the base against the honourable.

title: Isaiah 3:6
text: When a man shall take hold of his brother, in his father's house, [and shall say:] Thou hast clothing; be our chief, and let this ruin be under thy hand;

title: Isaiah 3:7
text: he will lift up [his hand] in that day, saying, I cannot be a healer, and in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; ye shall not make me a chief of the people.

title: Isaiah 3:8
text: For Jerusalem stumbleth and Judah falleth, because their tongue and their doings are against Jehovah, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

title: Isaiah 3:9
text: ¶The look of their face doth witness against them, and they declare their sin as Sodom: they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have brought evil upon themselves.

title: Isaiah 3:10
text: Say ye of the righteous that it shall be well [with him], for they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

title: Isaiah 3:11
text: Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill [with him], because the desert of his hands shall be rendered unto him.

title: Isaiah 3:12
text: [As for] my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. My people! they that guide thee mislead [thee], and destroy the way of thy paths.

title: Isaiah 3:13
text: Jehovah setteth himself to plead, and standeth to judge the peoples.

title: Isaiah 3:14
text: Jehovah will enter into judgment with the elders of his people and their princes, [saying:] It is ye that have eaten up the vineyard: the spoil of the poor is in your houses.

title: Isaiah 3:15
text: What mean ye that ye crush my people, and grind the faces of the afflicted? saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 3:16
text: ¶And Jehovah said, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched-out neck and wanton eyes, and go along mincing, and making a tinkling with their feet;

title: Isaiah 3:17
text: therefore the Lord will make bald the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and Jehovah will lay bare their secret parts.

title: Isaiah 3:18
text: In that day the Lord will take away the ornament of anklets, and the little suns and crescents,

title: Isaiah 3:19
text: the pearl-drops, and the bracelets, and the veils,

title: Isaiah 3:20
text: the head-dresses, and the stepping chains, and the girdles, and the scent-boxes, and the amulets;

title: Isaiah 3:21
text: the finger-rings, and the nose-rings;

title: Isaiah 3:22
text: the festival-robes, and the tunics, and the mantles, and the wallets;

title: Isaiah 3:23
text: the mirrors, and the fine linen bodices, and the turbans, and the flowing veils.

title: Isaiah 3:24
text: And it shall come to pass, instead of perfume there shall be rottenness; and instead of a girdle, a rope; and instead of well-set hair, baldness; and instead of a robe of display, a girding of sackcloth; brand instead of beauty.

title: Isaiah 3:25
text: Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the fight;

title: Isaiah 3:26
text: and her gates shall lament and mourn; and, stripped, she shall sit upon the ground.

title: Isaiah 4:1
text: ¶And seven women shall take hold of one man in that day, saying, Our own bread will we eat, and with our own garments will we be clothed; only let us be called by thy name; --take away our reproach!

title: Isaiah 4:2
text: ¶In that day there shall be a sprout of Jehovah for beauty and glory, and the fruit of the earth for excellency and for ornament for those that are escaped of Israel.

title: Isaiah 4:3
text: And it shall come to pass that he who remaineth in Zion, and he that is left in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, --every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem;

title: Isaiah 4:4
text: when the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have scoured out the blood of Jerusalem from its midst, by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.

title: Isaiah 4:5
text: And Jehovah will create over every dwelling-place of mount Zion, and over its convocations, a cloud by day and a smoke, and the brightness of a flame of fire by night: for over all the glory shall be a covering.

title: Isaiah 4:6
text: And there shall be a tabernacle for shade by day from the heat, and for a shelter and for a covert from storm and from rain.

title: Isaiah 5:1
text: ¶I will sing to my well-beloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard: My well-beloved had a vineyard upon a fruitful hill.

title: Isaiah 5:2
text: And he dug it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine; and he built a tower in the midst of it, and also hewed out a winepress therein; and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, but it brought forth wild grapes.

title: Isaiah 5:3
text: And now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, between me and my vineyard.

title: Isaiah 5:4
text: What was there yet to do to my vineyard that I have not done in it? Wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes, brought it forth wild grapes? --

title: Isaiah 5:5
text: And now, let me tell you what I am about to do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it shall be eaten up; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trodden under foot;

title: Isaiah 5:6
text: and I will make it a waste--it shall not be pruned nor cultivated, but there shall come up briars and thorns; and I will command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

title: Isaiah 5:7
text: For the vineyard of Jehovah of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah the plant of his delight: and he looked for justice, and behold, blood-shedding; for righteousness, and behold, a cry.

title: Isaiah 5:8
text: ¶Woe unto them that add house to house, that join field to field, until there is no more room, and that ye dwell yourselves alone in the midst of the land!

title: Isaiah 5:9
text: In mine ears Jehovah of hosts [hath said], Many houses shall assuredly become a desolation, great and excellent ones, without inhabitant.

title: Isaiah 5:10
text: Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield an ephah.

title: Isaiah 5:11
text: Woe unto them that, rising early in the morning, run after strong drink; that linger till twilight, [till] wine inflameth them!

title: Isaiah 5:12
text: And harp and lyre, tambour and flute, and wine are in their banquets; but they regard not the work of Jehovah, nor do they see the operation of his hands.

title: Isaiah 5:13
text: Therefore my people are led away captive from lack of knowledge, and their nobility die of famine, and their multitude are parched with thirst.

title: Isaiah 5:14
text: Therefore doth Sheol enlarge its desire, and open its mouth without measure; and her splendour shall descend [into it], and her multitude, and her tumult, and [all] that is joyful within her.

title: Isaiah 5:15
text: And the mean man shall be bowed down, and the great man brought low, and the eyes of the lofty shall be brought low;

title: Isaiah 5:16
text: and Jehovah of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy *God hallowed in righteousness.

title: Isaiah 5:17
text: And the lambs shall feed as on their pasture, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat.

title: Isaiah 5:18
text: ¶Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as with cart-ropes!

title: Isaiah 5:19
text: who say, Let him hasten, let him speed his work, that we may see [it]; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it!

title: Isaiah 5:20
text: Woe unto them who call evil good, and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!

title: Isaiah 5:21
text: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and intelligent in their own esteem!

title: Isaiah 5:22
text: Woe unto them that are mighty for drinking wine, and men valiant to mix strong drink;

title: Isaiah 5:23
text: who justify the wicked for a bribe, and turn away the righteousness of the righteous from them!

title: Isaiah 5:24
text: Therefore as a tongue of fire devoureth the stubble, and dry grass sinketh down in the flame, their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust; for they have rejected the law of Jehovah of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

title: Isaiah 5:25
text: Therefore is the anger of Jehovah kindled against his people, and he hath stretched out his hand against them and hath smitten them; and the mountains trembled, and their carcases are become as dung in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 5:26
text: And he will lift up a banner to the nations afar off, and will hiss for one from the end of the earth; and behold, it will come rapidly [and] lightly.

title: Isaiah 5:27
text: None among them is weary, none stumbleth; they slumber not, nor sleep; none hath the girdle of his loins loosed, nor the thong of his sandals broken;

title: Isaiah 5:28
text: their arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent; their horses' hoofs are reckoned as the flint, and their wheels as a whirlwind.

title: Isaiah 5:29
text: Their roaring is like a lioness, they roar as the young lions; yea, they growl, and snatch the prey, and carry it away safe, and there is none to deliver;

title: Isaiah 5:30
text: and they shall roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea. And if one look upon the earth, behold darkness [and] distress, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof.

title: Isaiah 6:1
text: ¶In the year of the death of king Uzziah, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

title: Isaiah 6:2
text: Seraphim were standing above him: each had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he flew.

title: Isaiah 6:3
text: And one called to the other and said, Holy, holy, holy is Jehovah of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory!

title: Isaiah 6:4
text: And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

title: Isaiah 6:5
text: ¶And I said, Woe unto me! for I am undone; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 6:6
text: And one of the seraphim flew unto me, and he had in his hand a glowing coal, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar;

title: Isaiah 6:7
text: and he made it touch my mouth, and said, Behold, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin expiated.

title: Isaiah 6:8
text: And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? And I said, Here am I; send me.

title: Isaiah 6:9
text: ¶And he said, Go; and thou shalt say unto this people, Hearing ye shall hear and shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see and shall not perceive.

title: Isaiah 6:10
text: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and blind their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and healed.

title: Isaiah 6:11
text: And I said, Lord, how long? And he said, Until the cities be wasted, without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land become an utter desolation,

title: Isaiah 6:12
text: and Jehovah have removed men far away, and the solitude be great in the midst of the land.

title: Isaiah 6:13
text: But a tenth part shall still be therein, and it shall return and be eaten; as the terebinth and as the oak whose trunk [remaineth] after the felling: the holy seed shall be the trunk thereof.

title: Isaiah 7:1
text: ¶And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, [that] Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to make war against it, but they were not able to fight against it.

title: Isaiah 7:2
text: And it was told the house of David saying, Syria is allied with Ephraim. Then his heart and the heart of his people shook, as the trees of the forest are shaken with the wind.

title: Isaiah 7:3
text: And Jehovah said to Isaiah, Go out now to meet Ahaz, thou and thy son Shear-jashub, at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the highway of the fuller's field;

title: Isaiah 7:4
text: and thou shalt say unto him, Take heed and be quiet; fear not, and let not thy heart faint before these two ends of smoking firebrands, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.

title: Isaiah 7:5
text: Inasmuch as Syria hath taken evil counsel against thee, Ephraim [also] and the son of Remaliah, saying,

title: Isaiah 7:6
text: Let us go up against Judah, and harass it, and make a breach therein for us, and set up a king therein--the son of Tabeal;

title: Isaiah 7:7
text: thus saith the Lord Jehovah: It shall not stand, nor come to pass;

title: Isaiah 7:8
text: for the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty-five years shall Ephraim be broken, so as to be no [more a] people;

title: Isaiah 7:9
text: and the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son. If ye believe not, surely ye shall not be established.

title: Isaiah 7:10
text: ¶And Jehovah spoke again to Ahaz, saying,

title: Isaiah 7:11
text: Ask for thee a sign from Jehovah thy God; ask for it in the deep, or in the height above.

title: Isaiah 7:12
text: And Ahaz said, I will not ask, and will not tempt Jehovah.

title: Isaiah 7:13
text: And he said, Hear then, house of David: Is it a small matter for you to weary men, that ye weary also my God?

title: Isaiah 7:14
text: Therefore will the Lord himself give you a sign: Behold, the virgin shall conceive and shall bring forth a son, and call his name Immanuel.

title: Isaiah 7:15
text: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and to choose the good.

title: Isaiah 7:16
text: For before the child knoweth to refuse the evil and to choose the good, the land whose two kings thou fearest shall be forsaken.

title: Isaiah 7:17
text: ¶Jehovah will bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father's house, days which have not come since the day when Ephraim turned away from Judah--[even] the king of Assyria.

title: Isaiah 7:18
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that Jehovah will hiss for the fly which is at the extremity of the streams of Egypt, and for the bee which is in the land of Assyria;

title: Isaiah 7:19
text: and they shall come and settle all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and on all thorn-bushes, and on all the pastures.

title: Isaiah 7:20
text: In that day will the Lord, with a razor which is hired beyond the river, with the king of Assyria, shave the head and the hair of the feet, yea, the beard also will it take away.

title: Isaiah 7:21
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] a man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep,

title: Isaiah 7:22
text: and it shall come to pass, from the abundance of milk they shall give, [that] he shall eat butter; for every one that remaineth in the midst of the land shall eat butter and honey.

title: Isaiah 7:23
text: And it shall come to pass in that day, [that] every place, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silver pieces, shall become briars and thorns:

title: Isaiah 7:24
text: with arrows and with the bow shall they come thither, for the whole land shall become briars and thorns.

title: Isaiah 7:25
text: And all mountains that have been dug up with the hoe--thither will they not come, from fear of briars and thorns; and they shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of small cattle.

title: Isaiah 8:1
text: ¶And Jehovah said to me, Take thee a great tablet, and write thereon with a man's style, concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

title: Isaiah 8:2
text: And I took unto me to witness, sure witnesses, Urijah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.

title: Isaiah 8:3
text: And I came near to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son; and Jehovah said unto me, Call his name, Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

title: Isaiah 8:4
text: For before the lad knoweth to cry, My father! and, My mother! the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria.

title: Isaiah 8:5
text: And Jehovah spoke again to me, saying,

title: Isaiah 8:6
text: Forasmuch as this people refuseth the waters of Shiloah which flow softly, and rejoiceth in Rezin and in the son of Remaliah,

title: Isaiah 8:7
text: therefore behold, the Lord will bring up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory; and he shall mount up over all his channels, and go over all his banks:

title: Isaiah 8:8
text: and he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow it and go further, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel!

title: Isaiah 8:9
text: ¶Rage, ye peoples, and be broken in pieces! And give ear, all ye distant parts of the earth: Gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, and be broken in pieces!

title: Isaiah 8:10
text: Settle a plan, and it shall come to nought; speak a word, and it shall not stand: for *God is with us.

title: Isaiah 8:11
text: For Jehovah spoke thus to me with a strong hand, and he instructed me not to walk in the way of this people, saying,

title: Isaiah 8:12
text: Ye shall not say, Conspiracy, of everything of which this people saith, Conspiracy; and fear ye not their fear, and be not in dread.

title: Isaiah 8:13
text: Jehovah of hosts, him shall ye sanctify; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.

title: Isaiah 8:14
text: And he will be for a sanctuary; and for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

title: Isaiah 8:15
text: And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and snared, and taken.

title: Isaiah 8:16
text: ¶Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.

title: Isaiah 8:17
text: And I will wait for Jehovah, who hideth his face from the house of Jacob; and I will look for him.

title: Isaiah 8:18
text: Behold, I and the children that Jehovah hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel, from Jehovah of hosts, who dwelleth in mount Zion.

title: Isaiah 8:19
text: And when they shall say unto you, Seek unto the necromancers and unto the soothsayers, who chirp and who mutter, [say,] Shall not a people seek unto their God? [Will they go] for the living unto the dead?

title: Isaiah 8:20
text: To the law and the testimony! If they speak not according to this word, for them there is no daybreak.

title: Isaiah 8:21
text: And they shall pass through it, hard pressed and hungry; and it shall come to pass when they are hungry, they will fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, and will gaze upward:

title: Isaiah 8:22
text: and they will look to the earth; and behold, trouble and darkness, gloom of anguish; and they shall be driven into thick darkness.

title: Isaiah 9:1
text: ¶Nevertheless the darkness shall not be as when the distress was in the [land], at the time he at first lightly, and afterwards heavily, visited the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, --the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:

title: Isaiah 9:2
text: the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light; they that dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, upon them light hath shone.

title: Isaiah 9:3
text: Thou hast multiplied the nation, hast increased its joy: they joy before thee like to the joy in harvest; as [men] rejoice when they divide the spoil.

title: Isaiah 9:4
text: For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.

title: Isaiah 9:5
text: For every boot of him that is shod for the tumult, and the garment rolled in blood, shall be for burning, fuel for fire.

title: Isaiah 9:6
text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder; and his name is called Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty *God, Father of Eternity, Prince of Peace.

title: Isaiah 9:7
text: Of the increase of his government and of peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it, and to uphold it with judgment and with righteousness, from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of Jehovah of hosts will perform this.

title: Isaiah 9:8
text: ¶The Lord sent a word unto Jacob, and it lighteth upon Israel.

title: Isaiah 9:9
text: And all the people shall know [it], Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in pride and stoutness of heart,

title: Isaiah 9:10
text: The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones; the sycamore trees are cut down, but we will replace them with cedars.

title: Isaiah 9:11
text: And Jehovah will set up the adversaries of Rezin against him, and arm his enemies,

title: Isaiah 9:12
text: the Syrians on the east, and the Philistines on the west; and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his anger is not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 9:13
text: But the people turneth not unto him that smiteth them, and they do not seek Jehovah of hosts.

title: Isaiah 9:14
text: And Jehovah will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm-branch and rush, in one day:

title: Isaiah 9:15
text: the ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.

title: Isaiah 9:16
text: For the guides of this people mislead [them]; and they that are guided by them are swallowed up.

title: Isaiah 9:17
text: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice in their young men, neither will he have mercy on their fatherless and on their widows; for every one is a hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

title: Isaiah 9:18
text: For wickedness burneth as a fire: it devoureth briars and thorns, and kindleth in the thickets of the forest, and they go rolling up like a pillar of smoke.

title: Isaiah 9:19
